title: Mesothelioma Lawyer Cost: Contingency Fees, Asbestos Trusts and VA Rules (2026)
description: How mesothelioma and asbestos lawyers charge, how bankruptcy trust payment percentages work, typical case costs, and VA fee rules for veterans.
h1: How much does a mesothelioma lawyer cost?
summary: Mesothelioma and other asbestos lawyers usually work on contingency, taking a percentage of lawsuit and trust recoveries and nothing if there is no recovery. Many claims are paid by asbestos bankruptcy trusts, which pay only a percentage of each claim's scheduled value (GAO's 2011 review found 1.1% to 100%). Veterans can also claim VA disability benefits, where representatives cannot charge before VA's initial decision and fee agreements paid from past-due benefits are capped at 20%.
body:
How mesothelioma and asbestos lawyers charge

Lawyers who represent people with mesothelioma or other asbestos diseases almost always work on contingency: a percentage of what is recovered, from lawsuits and from asbestos bankruptcy trusts, and no fee if nothing is recovered. The written agreement must state the percentage at each stage and whether expenses are deducted before or after the fee.[1] In states with general injury caps the cap applies here too; Michigan, for example, limits injury and wrongful death fees to one-third.[2]

Asbestos cases differ from ordinary injury cases in three ways that affect cost: there are often many defendants (product makers, suppliers, contractors), many of the original companies are bankrupt and pay through trusts instead of courts, and the exposure history may span decades and several states. Ask whether the firm charges the same percentage on trust claims as on lawsuits, because trust claims are paperwork-driven and may involve less work than a trial.

Asbestos bankruptcy trusts

When an asbestos company reorganizes in bankruptcy, it can set up a trust to pay current and future claimants. GAO counted 60 trusts established since 1988, holding about $37 billion in total assets, in its 2011 report.[3] That figure is from 2011; trust balances change every year as claims are paid.

Most trusts cannot pay every claim in full and still protect future claimants, so they set a payment percentage: a fraction of a claim's scheduled value that is actually paid. GAO gives the example of a $100,000 scheduled value at a 44% payment percentage, which pays $44,000.[3] The trust documents GAO reviewed specified payment percentages ranging from 1.1% to 100% for certain diseases, and GAO cited a 2010 RAND study putting the median at 25%.[3] Payment percentages are recalculated over time, so ask your lawyer for each trust's current figure rather than relying on these dated numbers.

Illustrative arithmetic only (hypothetical values, not a prediction). Suppose a claimant qualifies with three trusts whose scheduled values and payment percentages are $50,000 at 40%, $80,000 at 10% and $30,000 at 25%. Paid amounts: $20,000 + $8,000 + $7,500 = $35,500. At a one-third fee: $35,500 × 1/3 ≈ $11,833. At a 25% fee for trust-only work: $35,500 × 0.25 = $8,875. Difference: about $2,958 before costs.

What an asbestos lawsuit costs to build

Case costs are normally advanced by the firm and repaid from the recovery. Typical items include:

  • Work and exposure history: employment, union, Social Security earnings and military records to show where and when exposure happened.
  • Medical proof: pathology review of the diagnosis and a medical expert on causation.
  • Product identification: co-worker testimony, invoices, ship or building records, sometimes an industrial hygienist.
  • Depositions: often the patient's own testimony is recorded early, which adds transcript and videographer costs.
  • Filing in more than one place: where to sue depends on where exposure happened and where defendants can be sued, which can mean out-of-state counsel and local fees.

We could not find a reliable source for typical asbestos case expenses, so we do not publish a range. Ask each firm for its expected costs and whether you owe them if the case fails.[1]

Veterans: VA benefits and their fee rules

Many people with asbestos diseases were exposed in military service. VA disability compensation is a separate benefit from any lawsuit or trust claim. To qualify, the health condition must be caused by asbestos exposure and the veteran must have come into contact with asbestos during military service; VA asks for medical records, service records listing the job or specialty, and a doctor's statement linking the two.[4] VA lists jobs such as mining, milling, shipyards, construction, carpentry and demolition, and products including flooring, roofing, cement sheet, pipes, insulation and brake linings.[4]

Fees for VA claims are regulated by federal law: agents and attorneys may not charge for work done before the veteran receives notice of VA's initial decision, and a fee agreement paid directly from past-due benefits is capped at 20% of those benefits.[5] Accredited veterans service organizations help with initial claims. If a law firm offers to handle "VA benefits" as part of a mesothelioma case, ask exactly what it will do and charge on the VA side.

Deadlines

Asbestos diseases appear decades after exposure, so many states start the clock at diagnosis or discovery rather than exposure, but the rules differ and wrongful death claims have their own deadlines. Trusts set their own filing rules in their distribution procedures. The general injury deadline for each state is on its state page; get the asbestos-specific deadline confirmed by a lawyer soon after diagnosis.

Questions to ask before you sign

  • What percentage applies to lawsuits, and what to trust claims? Is there a lower rate for trust-only recoveries?
  • Will my case be referred to another firm, and how is the fee split between firms?
  • Which trusts do you expect to file with, and what are their current payment percentages?
  • Are costs deducted before or after the fee, and do I owe them if we lose?[1]
  • Will you handle my VA claim, and if so, how will you be paid under VA fee rules?[5]
Be wary of any firm or website that quotes an "average mesothelioma settlement" or promises a specific amount. Values depend on diagnosis, exposure evidence, defendants and trusts, and no one can know them before the case is investigated.

faq.q: How much does a mesothelioma lawyer charge?
faq.a: Usually a contingency fee, a percentage of the recovery from lawsuits and asbestos trusts, with no fee if nothing is recovered. Ask whether trust claims carry a lower percentage than litigated claims, and whether costs come out before or after the fee.

faq.q: What is an asbestos trust payment percentage?
faq.a: It is the share of a claim's scheduled value that a trust actually pays, set so the trust can also pay future claimants. GAO's 2011 report found ranges from 1.1% to 100% and cited a 2010 RAND median of 25%; current percentages are set by each trust.

faq.q: Can a veteran get VA benefits for mesothelioma?
faq.a: VA disability compensation is available when an asbestos-related condition is linked to contact with asbestos during military service. Representatives cannot charge for VA claim work before the initial decision, and fee agreements paid from past-due benefits are capped at 20%.

faq.q: Is an asbestos lawyer different from a mesothelioma lawyer?
faq.a: No. Mesothelioma is one asbestos disease; the same lawyers handle lung cancer, asbestosis and other asbestos claims under the same fee arrangements.
